title: Zoom-Through Cut
summary: Transition: rush into the first shot with zoom blur and burst out of the second.
description: A whip-zoom transition between two shots. Shot A accelerates toward the speaker with a growing radial zoom blur and a slight spin, hard-cuts at the peak, and shot B bursts out from extremely close, blurred, and decelerates back to normal framing. Use two clips (render with --second) or one clip split at `cutAt`. Shot A's captions blur away with the push; shot B gets its own caption style (tracked small caps by default).

options.cutAt: single-clip mode: where the cut happens (seconds or "@word"; "auto" = a word boundary near the middle). Ignored with --second (the cut is where clip A ends)
options.pushFrames: frames shot A spends rushing in before the cut (8-10 feels like the reference)
options.pullFrames: frames shot B takes to settle after the cut (10-14)
options.pushScale: how far shot A zooms in by the cut (4 = 4x)
options.blur: strength of the radial zoom blur (0 = none, 0.6 = strong)
options.samples: blur quality: copies used for the blur (6-9)
options.rotate: degrees of spin across the transition (0 = straight zoom)
options.focus: where shot A zooms: "chest" (default), "face", or [x, y] as 0-1 fractions
options.focusB: where shot B zooms out from (defaults to focus)
options.captionsA: caption overrides for shot A, e.g. {"style": "serif"}
options.captionsB: caption overrides for shot B, e.g. {"style": "tracked"}
